what_it_does: Microchips leak secrets through their power consumption: an attacker can measure how much current flows into a processor during encryption and reverse-engineer the secret key by analyzing power patterns. Existing defenses add randomization (masking) to make power signatures unpredictable, but they're either too expensive or don't eliminate all leakage. This paper proposes POLARIS, which uses explainable AI (machine learning that shows which patterns it learned) to automate the design of masking strategies. The system automatically builds a training dataset of actual power measurements without manual labeling, trains a masking model to obfuscate the most exploitable power patterns, and uses AI interpretability to pinpoint which signatures pose the highest risk. This makes masking more targeted and efficient than prior ad-hoc approaches.
